column.text: Bitcoin is back above $81,000 after dipping below $80,000, its lowest level since July. That flush left spot ETF holders, with an average cost basis near $81.5K, and corporate treasuries, near $80.2K, sitting on unrealized losses. Whether the reclaim holds is the question for the next session. Positioning is lopsided. Liquidations ran $26M on shorts against $2.3M on longs, which suggests the forced selling is largely done. Hyperliquid whales remain heavily net short, with BTC at -$801M and ETH at -$716M, yet lighter whale flow is buying ETH (+$1.77M) and US100 (+$3.1M). Daily BTC RSI sits at 46.61, leaving room to run, while 1h and 4h RSI at 65.86 and 56.43 flag intraday overheating. Flows are mixed. Tuesday's BTC ETF inflow was +$24.5M and ETH's was +$33.1M, both partial as issuers are still reporting, while SOL saw -$19.2M. On a 7-day basis, BTC is +$436.0M, ETH is -$276.2M, and SOL is -$45.0M. Fear & Greed reads 51, neutral. The tape is down-trending, but that alone is not a short signal. Shorts need a mechanism you can point to, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Continuation longs need real proof: rising open interest with price, a reclaim of the 20-day MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. Dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure has to decide this one. Hold $81K and the bullish case gains weight; lose it and the sub-$80K low comes back into play.
